panels.caption: Meet the macrophage. It is a helper cell in your body.
references: Macrophages are immune cells that engulf germs (Janeway et al., Immunobiology, 2001).

panels.caption: Uh oh. A germ shows up where the helper cells live.
The macrophage acts like a superhero. It wraps around the germ and swallows it up.
With the germ gone, the tissue is safe again. The helper cells get back to work.
